refresh_2026_11_07.scope: Extension of this file, arxiv-query.json, previous-audit-search-record.json and theorem-comparison.md (cutoff 5 November 2026) through 7 November 2026, focused on whether known results imply the candidate theorem or resolve the disk case of [ALL25] Question 4.9.
coverage: arXiv, 1 January 2025 to 7 November 2026: 60 API queries plus 14 queries on arXiv's separate HTML search, giving 1,211 distinct records; topical papers were read or grepped in full text.
arXiv, 22 February to 31 December 2024: 112 folding-related papers found and 111 grepped in full text; only [ALL25] itself matched.
The 5 November base query all:polyomino AND all:folding was re-run and returned the same 13 records (see rerun_2026_11_07 in arxiv-query.json).

Works citing [ALL25], as far as reachable: Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, OpenCitations, DataCite, zbMATH Open and full-text greps. The only citing work found is Lehner-Shirley, arXiv:2510.18197 [LS25], read end to end; it does not mention Question 4.9, Open Problem 9.2 (8.2 in the arXiv numbering), Theorem 8.2 or simply connected sources.
Full-text greps, each with a positive control: CCCG 2025 and 2026 (tentative proceedings), EuroCG 2024-2026, CG:YRF 2025, JCDCG^3 2026 and FWCG 2025.
Titles: SoCG 2025-2026, FUN 2026, WALCOM 2025-2026, ISAAC 2025, GD 2025-2026, JoCG 16-17 and CGTA since January 2025.
Origami^8 (8OSME): titles and Crossref-deposited reference lists of all 128 chapters (1,891 references); no chapter cites [ALL25] or [LS25].
Ten authors (Lehner, Lindorfer, Aichholzer, E. and M. Demaine, Akitaya, Kostitsyna, C. Schmidt, Fekete, Kleist): homepages or CVs where available, arXiv, ORCID and OpenAlex.
Theses (TU Graz IST database, IST Austria, Auckland ResearchSpace, MIT DSpace), German, Chinese and Japanese searches, and Stack Exchange.

Related works screened in full text (read or skimmed): Czajkowski et al., CCCG 2020; Akitaya-Demaine-Ku, Origami^8 Vol. III; Demaine-Devadoss-Mitchell-O'Rourke, CCCG 2004; Arkin et al. 2004; Melikhov, arXiv:1711.03518. See theorem-comparison.md.
findings: No prior or concurrent resolution of the disk case of [ALL25] Question 4.9 was found, and no known theorem implies the candidate. The published [ALL25] (JoCG, 16 November 2025) still lists Question 4.9 as open.

Already known: the tree case, essentially from [ALL25] Section 7, and the disks satisfying the hypothesis of [ALL25] Theorem 8.2. Many non-tree disks with a surjective map fail that hypothesis: the smallest have 8 cells (19 free shapes with all joins retained), and at 14 cells, with all joins retained, 215,762 of the 473,908 free non-tree disks with a surjective map fail it.

No individual instance is new: all 34,697 small witnesses (non-tree disks with a surjective map that fail the Theorem 8.2 hypothesis; all joins up to 12 cells, slits up to 10 cells) also fold by elementary moves, 34,648 (99.86%) by planar simple folds followed by folding a cube net and the other 49 by a multi-layer tree wrap whose certification relies on Theorem M3.

Related works identified and added to the manuscript's references: [CDD+20], [DW18] (unread; paywalled), [ADK26], [DDMO04], [ABD+04] and [Mel17]. None of those read implies the candidate; [DW18], which is unread, concerns only the 3x3 square.
access_failures: dblp: Anubis bot challenge; not bypassed.
Lens.org: search CAPTCHA; the API needs a token.
CORE: Cloudflare challenge; the API needs a key.
IA Scholar: anti-scrape challenge; not bypassed.
TU Graz thesis repositories: diglib refused the connection, PURE returned HTTP 403, and the Invenio repository failed its positive control.
Semantic Scholar: repeatedly rate-limited (HTTP 429); the JoCG DOI is not indexed there.
Dunham-Whieldon chapter: paywalled; full text not obtained.
Not covered: CCCG 2024 (not checked), the JCDCG^3 2025 programme (unreachable), work under review, and the [ALL25] authors (not asked).

decision_problem_search_2026_11_09.scope: Whether a polynomial-time algorithm for CubeFolding restricted to simply connected polyominoes (the disk case of [ALL25] Conjecture 4.10) was already known.
decision_problem_search_2026_11_09.record: ../../disk-folding-checks/9-poly-time/lit/search-log.json and NOTE.md, section Literature (outside this package).
decision_problem_search_2026_11_09.finding: No source found settles the disk case or gives a polynomial-time algorithm for simply connected polyominoes whose cell-adjacency graphs have cycles, in the [ALL25] model. The tree case is polynomial by the classification of [ALL25, Section 7]; [LS25, Section 1] says so explicitly. [ABDD18, Theorem 5] gives linear-time algorithms for tree-shaped sources onto polycubes with O(1) cubes in a different folding model. A citing-work search found [LS25] as the only work citing [ALL25].
decision_problem_search_2026_11_09.consequence: Corollary A2 of the manuscript is credited as new for disks with cycles; the Introduction credits the tree case to [ALL25, Section 7] and [LS25].

refresh_2026_11_09_night.finding: Nothing found that states, implies, contradicts or concurrently claims either result. The published [ALL25] (issued 16 November 2025) still lists Question 4.9, Conjecture 4.10 and Open Problem 9.2 as open; its only citing work found is [LS25]. [AAAC21, Section 4.3] says that every surjective consistent mapping its authors tried could be folded and that they could not prove this in general. The simply connected examples reported as non-foldable in the grid model ([ABDD18] Figure 13, Theorem 4 and Table 1) have no surjective consistent mapping; a recount of the Table 1 dual trees for 6 to 9 squares gives exactly its foldable counts 11, 114, 746 and 3768.
